title: SpaceX Reportedly In Talks To Supply Pentagon With AI Computing Power Worth Billions
source_used: Stocktwits (read in full), relaying The Wall Street Journal
key_facts: The Wall Street Journal reported that SpaceX is in talks to give the Pentagon data-centre capacity for running AI models at a cost of up to several billion dollars.
People familiar with the matter told the Journal the talks could collapse with no deal.
Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Oracle already provide capacity to the Pentagon.
A deal would give the Department of Defense more cloud-computing resources for AI applications across the National Security Agency and warfighters.
SpaceX plans a major expansion of its cloud computing, including competing with providers such as CoreWeave on price.
SpaceX acquired Elon Musk's xAI earlier this year and went public in June; Grok models and data centres sit in a segment called SpaceXAI.
SpaceX has cloud-computing deals with Anthropic, Google and Reflection AI, and all contracts allow early termination (per Stocktwits).
The Stocktwits page metadata is dated 17 Jul 2026, not 11 Oct; the WSJ date is not stated.
quote_evidence: According to a report from the Wall Street Journal, the two sides are negotiating an arrangement under which SpaceX would provide computing capacity to the department at a cost of up to several billion dollars.
Talks could collapse with no deal, people familiar with the matter told the Journal.
Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Oracle already provide capacity to the Pentagon.
why_it_matters_hint: Another large cloud supplier for US defence AI, though the talks could collapse.
event_date: Stocktwits page created 17 Jul 2026; WSJ publication date not stated.
notes: Older news re-dated: Stocktwits page metadata (created_at) says 17 Jul 2026, three months before the Google News date of 11 Oct. WSJ original not read. Relay, with the WSJ as first reporter.
